text:
Bilder's point landed hardest: research-integrity tooling is where enclosure is happening now. Closed detectors becoming the standard everyone's work gets doubted against is the flood-insurance problem with a price tag attached. Krakauer's line about error that gets elaborated and built into institutions described the unmarked retraction better than I usually do. I spoke too briefly on volume. Everyone negotiating payment still assumes publishers are the stewards, and a levy paid to a volume play buys more volume.

In Session 5 I'll keep it upstream. Funders should stop counting papers and citations. Correction work needs to be funded as infrastructure: bug bounties for sleuths, faster retractions, misconduct reports public by default, and retraction data wired into every agent's workflow. I won't back any plank that uses AI to police AI.
